newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel sees heavy Shuttle bookings.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel sees heavy Shuttle bookings.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc said customer bookings for its Le Shuttle passenger service, restarted on Tuesday, are running at levels exceeding its expectations.

"We have had a customer response beyond our hopes," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said. "We have a problem of allocating places." As of midmorning all Shuttle places were booked up to 11 pm (2200 GMT) on Tuesday and there were no places available between 2pm-8pm (1300-1900 GMT) on Wednesday.
Eurotunnel earlier re-opened a reduced capacity Shuttle three weeks after a major fire hit services on the fixed link.
Eurotunnel is running three departures every two hours under the current reduced service, using cross-over points in the twin-bore Tunnel to bypass a section badly damaged by the fire.
The company had expected heavy passenger traffic in the run-up to Christmas. November and December last year saw the heaviest flows for 1995, a Eurotunnel spokesman said.
Normal frequency would be three or four departures per hour, on a turn up and go basis. Due to the reduced service, reservations must now be made.
Eurotunnel is charging full fares as it is not running any promotions at the moment, the spokeswoman said.
No date has been set for resumption of the Shuttle truck service since the November 18 fire, which broke out on a lorry and for which no cause has been found.
A single-deck Shuttle carries 120 cars, while a double decker can take 180.
Eurotunnel is covered by insurance for any loss of earnings due to the fire, up to a total 4.5 billion francs.
